answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and registers one mesa beacon post above a lagoon. In each tide window it must sign in with its own key, making a tide stamp. An auditor checks each stamp against the log and lagoon tide table: a missing sign-in, a late stamp, or one operator signing for many identities in one window burns the bond. The first window costs 38 credits, the kth 38+6(k-1); the 1,000th costs 6,032, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,035,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-beacon ring fails because one key cannot make 1,000 in-window proofs. An honest identity pays 38 once, recovers its bond.
